items.description: The generated-index exclusion assertion cannot detect an index manifest entry.
items.evidence: tests/test_manifest.py:24 checks line.endswith('/index.json'), but every manifest line ends with its SHA-256 checksum.
items.analysis: The assertion always passes for a syntactically valid manifest line, including a line for skills/specle/index.json. It therefore does not demonstrate Requirement 1.3's generated-resource exclusion.
items.recommendation: Assert that no generated-index path is present in the generated lines, such as '/index.json:' not occurring in any line.
items.decision_rationale: The manifest must exclude the generated index, and the test should demonstrate that boundary.

items.description: The change brief's verification section still describes removed installed-manifest work.
items.evidence: .specle/changes/add-specle-manifest/spec.md:13 requires stale-manifest detection, installation/update distribution, and live-file drift validation.
items.analysis: The approved requirements deliberately make the manifest release-only and exclude it from init, installed-target validation, and update implementation. The brief should not describe verification for work this change explicitly excludes.
items.recommendation: Replace the stale verification list with the release-only command, append-only history, boundary, and quality-gate checks already specified by the requirements and design.
items.decision_rationale: The brief must match the approved release-only boundary and current requirements.

items.description: The manifest tests do not exercise appending missing entries to an existing valid manifest.
items.evidence: tests/test_manifest.py:27-37 creates an absent output, then reruns with the same complete inventory; it never starts from a valid partial or prior-version manifest.
items.analysis: Requirement 2.4 requires preserving existing history while appending only missing identities. The current test covers creation and a no-op, but not the production append path that rewrites an existing manifest with retained and new entries.
items.recommendation: Seed a valid manifest with one existing entry, invoke generation, and assert the original line remains exactly once while all missing current-version entries are appended.
items.decision_rationale: Append-only generation must preserve prior valid entries while adding missing inventory records.

items.description: The manifest tests do not demonstrate rejection of duplicate valid resource identities.
items.evidence: tests/test_manifest.py:40-61 exercises conflicting and malformed entries only; there is no valid duplicate `(version, path)` fixture.
items.analysis: Requirement 3.2 explicitly requires duplicate resource identities to be rejected before output replacement. The implementation has a duplicate check, but the specified externally observable failure behaviour is not covered.
items.recommendation: Seed two identical valid entries, assert ManifestError for a duplicate identity, and assert the manifest remains unchanged.
items.decision_rationale: Duplicate identity rejection is an explicit manifest contract and needs observable production coverage.

items.description: Manifest generation can overwrite an existing predictable temporary path.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:54-57 writes directly to .<output-name>.tmp before replacing the output.
items.analysis: An existing file is truncated, and an existing symlink is followed, before atomic replacement. This can alter unrelated user data selected only by a temporary-name collision.
items.recommendation: Create a unique temporary file securely in the output directory before replacement.
items.decision_rationale: Use exclusive creation for a unique temporary file in the output directory so no pre-existing path is overwritten.

items.description: Concurrent manifest generation can lose appended inventory records.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:42-57 performs an unlocked read-modify-write operation.
items.analysis: Separate processes can read the same prior contents then replace the output independently, leaving only one set of additions.
items.recommendation: Serialize each output's read-modify-write operation and use a unique temporary file.
items.decision_rationale: Concurrent manifest generation is outside the intended release-preparation workflow.

items.description: Manifest generation accepts a packaged inventory with completeness diagnostics.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:107-110 scans the package then calls append_manifest without checking inventory.package_diagnostics.
items.analysis: A package missing required managed content could produce incomplete release provenance while the command reports success.
items.recommendation: Reject inventory package diagnostics before generating a manifest.
items.decision_rationale: The command is intentionally a simple maintainer release-preparation tool; this additional completeness gate is not required.

items.description: Existing current-version entries for removed resources are not detected.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:45-51 checks generated identities against existing entries but does not compare existing current-version paths to the current inventory.
items.analysis: A manifest generated before a resource removal can retain that resource for the same version, so its version-filtered entries no longer reconstruct the intended inventory.
items.recommendation: Reject current-version entries that are absent from the supplied inventory.
items.decision_rationale: Release entries are append-only; generation does not reinterpret or remove recorded current-version paths.

items.description: A manifest output inside a managed skill resource tree can create a checksum cycle.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:107-110 scans all managed skill resources before writing the user-selected output path.
items.analysis: A later scan includes the generated manifest as a managed resource, making its own checksum unstable and conflicting with its recorded entry.
items.recommendation: Reject outputs within scanned managed resource trees.
items.decision_rationale: Output placement is an explicit maintainer choice; this command will not impose an additional path restriction.

items.description: Invalid UTF-8 in an existing manifest escapes as an unhandled traceback.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:67 reads text but catches OSError only.
items.analysis: UnicodeDecodeError is not converted to the command's documented ManifestError path.
items.recommendation: Catch UnicodeDecodeError and raise a path-specific ManifestError.
items.decision_rationale: Manifest documents are expected to be valid UTF-8, but an invalid file should produce a concise path-specific command error rather than a traceback.

items.description: The manifest parser accepts non-canonical resource paths.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:11-15 accepts arbitrary non-colon path components after a skill or policies prefix.
items.analysis: Traversal or malformed components can remain as provenance identities and distort comparison or query results.
items.recommendation: Validate canonical blueprint-relative paths before accepting existing entries.
items.decision_rationale: No additional path-normalisation layer is needed for this simple line-oriented release record.

items.description: Manifest generation replaces an output symlink rather than updating its target.
items.evidence: src/specle/manifest.py:67 reads through an output symlink, while line 57 replaces the symlink path itself.
items.analysis: The command can report success while the original target stays stale, contrary to the behaviour a user selecting that symlink path would ordinarily expect.
items.recommendation: Resolve the output path before reading and replacement, or preserve the symlink while updating its target.
items.decision_rationale: The explicit output path is replaced as selected; symlink-preservation semantics are not needed for this command.

items.description: Manifest generation reads a separately hard-coded package version.
items.evidence: src/specle/__init__.py:3 defines __version__ = '0.1.0'; src/specle/main.py:105-106 uses it for manifest entries.
items.analysis: A release version bump can leave the literal stale, misattributing immutable provenance entries to the wrong version.
items.recommendation: Use distribution metadata as the sole version source.
items.decision_rationale: The hard-coded version is a real defect and must be replaced with the installed distribution metadata source.

items.description: Tests do not prove generated manifest lines cover the complete supplied inventory.
items.evidence: tests/test_manifest.py:17-24 checks two sample lines; tests/test_main.py:84-90 checks only file creation and output wording.
items.analysis: A line-builder omission for another resource could pass the current tests, despite the manifest contract requiring a complete inventory.
items.recommendation: Assert generated paths exactly equal all skill and policy resource paths in the supplied inventory, and verify CLI output against that complete set.
items.decision_rationale: Representative production checks are sufficient for this simple release-preparation command; exhaustive inventory duplication is not required.
